security_review.reason: Required from THIS registration's start, not carved as an exception: the second registration's own security_review.reason contained a material measurement error, corrected here. That reason claimed 'the pre-existing message already interpolates the full stringified error... nothing newly reaches a consumer the message did not already carry' -- FALSE. Measured 2026-08-01: String(error) (the OLD, pre-any-of-this-slice's-work path) renders only the top-level `"${name}: ${message}"`. What migrate.ts's CLI now prints via console.error(wrappingError) additionally surfaces the ENTIRE pg DatabaseError shape via Node's default .cause-recursive formatting: severity, code, detail, hint, position, internalPosition, internalQuery, where, schema, table, column, dataType, constraint, file, line, routine. The earlier claim conflated 'the error object's enumerable key set' (correctly measured: no .client, no credentials) with 'what String(error) actually renders' (a much narrower thing, never separately verified until this registration) -- two different measurements collapsed into one. Worse: `detail` specifically is NOT schema/DDL-shaped like the rest of that list -- on a unique-violation Postgres populates it with the OFFENDING ROW'S ACTUAL VALUES, e.g. `Key (email)=(user@example.com) already exists.`. A migration performing a data backfill against tables like persons/accounts/channel_identities would print real PII into deployment logs. That collides directly with this repository's own HARD RULE that money/PII never reaches a public surface (docs/00-start-here/HANDOFF.md). This is why the review is required on the merits, not merely because a prior review round asked for it: a privileged deployment surface's logging behavior changed, and the change was motivated by a real, previously-mismeasured PII exposure path. The fix in this registration (see negative_scope) is an explicit field allowlist at the CLI sink, keeping schema-identifying fields (code/severity/constraint/table/column/routine/file/line) and dropping row-shaped ones (detail/hint/internalQuery/where). `.cause` itself is unchanged and correct.
